web-pages.cloud.inviteSignIn: You're invited to a {name} workspace. Sign in with Google, then choose whether to join.
web-pages.cloud.noWorkspaceBody: Ask someone using {name} to invite {email}, or create your own.

web-pages.cloud.slackInstalled.doneBody: Back in {name}, add the app's App-Level Token on the Connects page to finish. You can close this page.
web-pages.cloud.slackInstalled.notInstal: Slack didn't allow the install. Go back to {name} and click “Install to workspace” again.

web-pages.connect.bothRuntimes: Runs on both runtimes. The runtime is fixed after creation.
web-pages.connect.chooseLead: Messages to “{name}” will go to the chosen session. The old session is kept but gets nothing new from this connect.
web-pages.connect.deleteBody: Disconnects from Slack. Delete the app in Slack yourself.

web-pages.connect.deleteBodySessions.one: Disconnects from Slack. Its 1 session keeps its history but gets no new messages. Delete the app in Slack yourself.
web-pages.connect.deleteBodySessions.other: Disconnects from Slack. Its {n} sessions keep their history but get no new messages. Delete the app in Slack yourself.

web-pages.connect.effects.mentionOnly: Only @-mentioned threads go into the session. Replies in threads already in it still arrive.
web-pages.connect.effects.newSingle: The next message starts a new single session. You can also pick an existing one after switching.
web-pages.connect.effects.noMention: No @ needed: every message in channels and DMs it can see goes to the agent. Usage goes up noticeably.
web-pages.connect.effects.resumeSingle: Resumes the single session it was bound to.

web-pages.connect.effects.running.one: 1 session is running and will finish its current turn.
web-pages.connect.effects.running.other: {n} sessions are running and will finish their current turn.

web-pages.connect.effects.switchBack: Switching back to single session resumes the same one.
web-pages.connect.effects.threadsRestart: To continue a thread from the single session, @ it again. That starts a new session without the old context.
web-pages.connect.effects.toMulti: The bound session stops getting messages. Each thread gets its own session when @-mentioned.
web-pages.connect.effects.toSingle: All messages go into one session. Existing per-thread sessions stop getting messages, including replies in their threads. History is kept.
web-pages.connect.everyMessageSentence: Every message it sees goes into the session.
web-pages.connect.made.appToken: On the Socket Mode page, generate an App-Level Token and copy it (starts with xapp-; scopes are preset).
web-pages.connect.made.manual: App created. Install it to the workspace, then copy the Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-…) from the OAuth page.
web-pages.connect.made.oauth: App created. Install it to the workspace and click “Allow” in Slack; the bot token goes to the station automatically.
web-pages.connect.manualApp: Create the app in Slack and paste tokens
web-pages.connect.mentionOff: Every message it sees in channels goes into the session.
web-pages.connect.mentionOn: Replies in an @-mentioned thread need no further @.
web-pages.connect.modeLead: Changes which session each message goes into. Ongoing chats may be cut off, so check the effects below.
web-pages.connect.noSession: No session yet. The next message starts one.
web-pages.connect.ownerLead: Decides whose “Created by me” it appears in. Owners, admins and the current owner can change it.
web-pages.connect.recentNone: No sessions yet. @{name} in Slack to start one.
web-pages.connect.replaceLead: Replace either one. Leave the other empty to keep it.
web-pages.connect.runtimeNote: Runs on {runtime}, fixed after creation; for another runtime, create a new connect. Sessions in progress keep their starting settings.
web-pages.connect.teamLead: Which Slack workspace's configuration token creates the app.
web-pages.connect.tokenWhy: With it, {name} creates the Slack app for you: set its name, avatar and permissions here instead of in Slack's admin. Only you can use it; others on this station can't see it.
web-pages.connects.about: A connect is how people reach {name}, such as a Slack app. Each lives on a station and is bound to a model.
web-pages.connects.addFirstLead: A connect lets people @ an agent in Slack: a Slack app hooked up to a station.
web-pages.connects.noOnline: No station online. Add one once it's back.
web-pages.connects.profileFirstLead: Connects run models through a profile. Add one first.
web-pages.connects.removeBody: Removes it from {name} only. The app stays in Slack; delete it in Slack's app settings if unused.
web-pages.errors.inviteCodeInvalid: Invalid invite code. Check for typos
web-pages.errors.inviteCodeRequired: The free plan includes 1 workspace; creating another needs an invite code
web-pages.errors.tooManyMembers: Member limit reached: just you on the free plan, up to 6 people on Standard
web-pages.errors.tooManyWorkspaces: An account can create up to 5 workspaces
web-pages.notifications.badge.allNote: Turns done that you have not read count too
web-pages.notifications.badge.attentionN: And chats you started that went wrong (the default)
web-pages.notifications.badge.decisionsN: What waits for your decision in 奏

web-pages.notifications.badge.title: What the badge counts

web-pages.notifications.kinds.doneNote: An agent finished and you have not read it
web-pages.notifications.kinds.failedNote: A turn failed, or an agent could not start
web-pages.notifications.kinds.messageNot: Someone else writes in a chat you take part in

web-pages.notifications.kinds.waitNote: An agent stopped for you: a card, or it needs your help

web-pages.notifications.noteDevice: Alerts you when an agent in your chats finishes, needs you or fails, or someone speaks. Not for the open chat. This device only (also allow {name} in System Settings)
web-pages.notifications.sound: Sound is the system's: System Settings → Notifications → {name} → Play sound for notifications.
web-pages.notifications.title: Chat alerts
web-pages.profiles.addModelPlaceholder: Add a model by name, e.g. qwen3.8-flash
web-pages.profiles.backgroundOff: New messages wait until the running command or subagent finishes.

web-pages.profiles.choice.anthropicApiLe: An Anthropic API key, runs Claude Code.
web-pages.profiles.choice.chatgptSubLead: ChatGPT Plus / Pro, runs Codex. Sign in once with a device code.
web-pages.profiles.choice.claudeSubLead: Claude Pro / Max, runs Claude Code. Sign in once in the browser.
web-pages.profiles.choice.envLead: Set env variables for your model service.
web-pages.profiles.choice.opencodeGoLead: One key for both Claude Code and Codex.
web-pages.profiles.copyFailed: Couldn't copy. Type the code in

web-pages.profiles.envLead: The runtime starts with these to reach your model service. {route} in a value becomes the session's route ID.
web-pages.profiles.fastLead: For sessions following the subscription. Fast uses more quota or credits
web-pages.profiles.keychainTip: This sign-in is in a keychain the station can't read. Sign in once for {name}; the machine's own sign-in is unaffected
web-pages.profiles.lead: What agents use to run models: {subscription} or a model service key.
web-pages.profiles.machineAdded: Profile added with this machine's sign-in
web-pages.profiles.machineLoginAbout: To switch accounts, sign in again or sign out, use {runtime} on this machine; this profile follows. To stop using it, disable it (top-right menu).
web-pages.profiles.manual: Or sign in on the server by hand
web-pages.profiles.modelsAbout: Only enabled models can be picked for new chats and connects.
web-pages.profiles.modelsAboutNone: After the profile is checked, its models appear here. Enable them to use them.

web-pages.settings.members.addedNote.other: {n} people · Join on first sign-in to {name}

web-pages.settings.workspace.deleteConfi.other: All members lose access, and {n} stations disconnect from {name} cloud (their data stays).

web-pages.slackApp.group.base.descriptio: Get @-mentions, read messages in its channels, DMs and group chats, and reply. Required.
web-pages.slackApp.group.canvases.descri: Create, edit and read canvases, e.g. plans and reports in a channel.
web-pages.slackApp.group.channels.descri: Create channels, invite members, and see joins and new channels.
web-pages.slackApp.group.connect.descrip: View, send and accept invites to channels shared with other companies.
web-pages.slackApp.group.customize.descr: Set a display name and avatar per message.
web-pages.slackApp.group.dm.description: Open DMs with one or more people.
web-pages.slackApp.group.extras.descript: Unfurl links, set reminders, read DND and call status.
web-pages.slackApp.group.files.descripti: Read attachments, upload screenshots, logs and other files.
web-pages.slackApp.group.lists.descripti: Create, edit and read Slack Lists, e.g. task lists.
web-pages.slackApp.group.more.descriptio: Set its presence, read message metadata and workspace settings, embed video links, handle slash commands.
web-pages.slackApp.group.people.descript: Read emails, profiles, user groups, workspace info and custom emoji.
web-pages.slackApp.group.public.descript: Reply in public channels without an invite.
web-pages.slackApp.group.reactions.descr: Mark progress with emoji, pin messages, manage bookmarks.

web-pages.slackApp.group.topics.descript: Set topics and purposes of channels and DMs, and invite people to channels.
web-pages.slackApp.group.usergroups.desc: Create user groups, edit members, start and update Slack calls.

web-pages.slackApp.needsTokenNote: It's yours only. Others on this station can't see it.
web-pages.slackApp.noApp: Can't find this connect's Slack app ({error}). Switch to a valid token and retry.
web-pages.slackApp.notConnected: Connect to Slack to edit its app here.
web-pages.slackApp.refreshPrefix: The Refresh Token starts with xoxe-1-.

web-pages.slackApp.step2Note: Scroll to “Your App Configuration Tokens” at the bottom, click Generate Token, and pick this workspace.
web-pages.slackApp.step3Note: Slack gives two tokens; use the lower one (xoxe-1-…). {name} renews it, so this is one-time.
web-pages.slackApp.updatedApprove: Updated. Approve new permissions in Slack
web-pages.stations.away: Offline: open {name} on that machine to reconnect

web-pages.stations.silent: Not responding: {name} cloud says it's online, but its status can't be read. It may be offline or asleep

web-pages.workspace.createLead: A workspace is a group of people and the stations they share. You'll own it.
web-pages.workspace.empty.body: Add one in {link}: run a command on the machine that will run {name}.

web-pages.profiles.share.futureIn: Stations added later can use it too
web-pages.profiles.share.futureOut: Stations added later are not added
web-pages.profiles.share.copy: This profile is shared by {station}; change it there.
web-pages.profiles.share.hostAway: {station} is not answering; it can't be used now

web-pages.dock.unreadNote: Off, only what waits on you and what failed
